changelog: Core Principles: added a short, positive criterion to favour boundaries that follow disambiguating heads (main verb, head noun, completed complement or a closing appositive) because they reduce premature commitments.

When to Segment: expanded surface-form signals to call out exclusives/negators (only, without), auxiliaries/adverbs that often await a verb (still, taking the), and appositive/name introducers (called, known as) as signals to lower confidence; kept candidacy generous rather than forbidding.

Priority Rules: added a specific demotion for comma-adjacent cuts when the continuation contains contrastive markers (not, only, rather than, without) or parallel items, and explicitly promote boundaries that come after a main predicate + core arguments or after a clearly closed appositive.

Decision Procedure: if the candidate set is smaller than the minimum required by [Output Rules], add extra low-confidence candidates at safe punctuation or clause boundaries and rank them last so format violations are avoided without forcing risky high-ranked cuts.
